s1.syndrome_frame: Acute kidney injury with proteinuria and hematuria in a patient with a left ventricular assist device
salient_findings: Increased serum creatinine from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months
Urinary protein excretion of 2.2 g/day with microhaematuria
Positive blood cultures for Corynebacterium jeikeium
key_facts: 55-year-old man with severe dilated cardiomyopathy
Left ventricular assist device (LVAD; HeartMate II) implanted four years previously
Admitted for evaluation of low-grade fever
Serum creatinine increased from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months
Urinary protein excretion of 2.2 g/day
Microhaematuria without dysmorphic erythrocytes or casts
Elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin
Low serum complement C3 concentrations
Elevated PR3-ANCA and rheumatoid factor concentrations
Negative anti-MPO-ANCA
Multiple foci of increased metabolic activity at the LVAD driveline insertion site, the ventricular assist device pocket, and the LVAD outflow cannula on 18F-FDG PET-CT

shortlist.label: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has low-grade fever, elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, and positive blood cultures for Corynebacterium jeikeium, suggesting an infectious cause for the glomerulonephritis

shortlist.label: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Renal biopsy shows segmental sclerotic glomeruli with increased mesangial matrix and mesangial cells, consistent with membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis

shortlist.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated PR3-ANCA concentrations, which is a specific marker for ANCA-associated vasculitis, and has symptoms consistent with this condition, such as renal involvement and low-grade fever

shortlist.label: Device-related infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has an LVAD and multiple foci of increased metabolic activity at the LVAD driveline insertion site, the ventricular assist device pocket, and the LVAD outflow cannula on 18F-FDG PET-CT, suggesting a device-related infection

shortlist.label: C3 glomerulopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Renal biopsy shows positive mesangial staining for C3 and low serum complement C3 concentrations, consistent with C3 glomerulopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's renal biopsy shows mesangial proliferation, increased mesangial matrix, and segmental sclerotic lesions, which are characteristic of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. Additionally, the immunohistology results show positive mesangial staining for IgM, C1q, and C3, and electron microscopy reveals mesangial regions with increased matrix and segmental subendothelial and mesangial osmiophilic deposits, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
rejected.why: The presence of low serum complement C3 concentrations and the lack of dysmorphic erythrocytes or casts in the urine make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated PR3-ANCA concentrations, the renal biopsy findings and the presence of device-related infection suggest a different primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Device-related infection
rejected.why: While the patient has a device-related infection, this is not a primary diagnosis for the renal findings

rejected.label: C3 glomerulopathy
rejected.why: The patient's renal biopsy shows a more complex pattern of injury, including mesangial proliferation and segmental sclerotic lesions, which is not typical of C3 glomerulopathy

gold: Focal segmental necrotising immune-complex glomerulonephritis triggered by chronic LVAD infection with Corynebacterium jeikeium
